subject: general
question: What is the minimum age for employment in factories or mines or other hazardous employment, according to Article 24 of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __14 years.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 24__ of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any other hazardous employment.
 
• This provision is aimed at safeguarding children from exploitation and ensuring their health and development.
 
• The law applies to hazardous work environments and ensures strict enforcement to prevent child labor.
 
• Violation of this law attracts penalties under the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, and other related legislations.
 
• The aim is to promote education and child welfare by preventing underage employment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Labour Prohibition:**

 
 
• The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in hazardous occupations and processes.
 
• It also regulates conditions of work for children in non-hazardous occupations.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education:**
 
 
• The Right to Education Act, 2009, ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This complements the prohibition of child labor by promoting education and literacy.
 
 
 
• **National Policies:**
 
 
• The National Policy on Child Labour, 1987, focuses on the rehabilitation of children removed from hazardous labor environments.
 
• The policy includes measures for education, health, and social welfare of affected children.
